brief: The Market Ear lists five bullish forces it says are lining up for stocks. First, a valuation reset: Scott Rubner notes the S&P 500 semiconductor index trades at 13.8x forward earnings, a 25% discount to the broader market and the widest since December 2018; Peter Callahan puts the SOX's forward P/E discount near 15-year wides; Citadel says the Nasdaq 100's forward P/E has fallen to about 19x, near 2022 bear-market levels, though the index is not currently in a bear market. Second, mega-cap leadership: Microsoft printed a fresh all-time high and Apple surged over 5% Wednesday, its best session in 18 months. Third, an energy tailwind: per Goldman's trading desk, Brent has plunged roughly $18 in five sessions; Javier Blas notes US wholesale gasoline hit a seven-month low, which could boost consumers heading into the holidays if sustained. Fourth, Goldman Sachs' FICC and Equities desk says buyback authorizations hit a record $1.3 trillion, over 10% above 2025, with companies in open repurchase windows set to rise from roughly 300 to nearly 500. Fifth, GS Market Data and Sean Emory cite post-midterm and presidential-cycle seasonality as historically strong for the S&P 500 into next year.
